criteria-objective.reason: RE-ATTESTED 2026-08-28 after ACC-0037 was authored and ACC-0020 was superseded — re-evaluated rather than carried forward, the same treatment this criterion has had at every previous change. ⚠️ ACC-0037 IS OBJECTIVE, and it is narrower than the criterion it replaces: a p95 over 50 measured samples of one named span (`compileStageDocument`), on a named document, after ten discarded warm-ups, with a counter that must advance exactly once per measured request. Every clause is a number or a count; none of them is a reading. The VOID condition is objective too, and it has been falsified rather than assumed — memoising the compiler makes the harness refuse to report timings at all. ⚠️ THE SUPERSESSION IS WHAT THIS RE-ATTESTATION IS REALLY ABOUT, and it makes the stage's criteria MORE objective rather than less. ACC-0020 bounded read-plus-compile at 300 ms; six valid runs split 3/3 across that line, which means it could not decide its own question on the reference host. A criterion whose verdict flips between identical runs is not pass/fail without a judgement call, whatever its wording says. Its successor bounds a span that measured 15-29 ms against a 50 ms ceiling — a margin that does not turn on ambient load. ⚠️ ACC-0020 REMAINS `fail` AND REMAINS READABLE. It is retired, not deleted, it names its successor, and DEC-0025 records what was concluded. The stage does not become objective by removing the criterion that was hard to decide. ⚠️ WHAT THIS STILL DOES NOT CLAIM: ACC-0029 and ACC-0030 remain `not-evaluated` because no browser was available, and five shell criteria are unevaluated in total. This stage says its criteria are decidable, not that they have all been decided.
